stem: How was the U.S. economy affected during World War I?
visual_elements: Entry into the war in 1917 unleashed massive U.S. federal spending which shifted national production from civilian to war goods. Between 1914 and 1918, some 3 million people were added to the military and half a million to the government.
—Carlos Lozada, “The Economics of World War I,” National Bureau of Economic Research, January 2005
